headline: Brand distils phosphorus
detail: A Hamburg alchemist boils down urine looking for gold and finds a glowing white solid - the first element with a named discoverer.

headline: Brandt isolates cobalt
detail: The first metal discovered since antiquity breaks the ancient list of seven.

headline: Cavendish weighs inflammable air
detail: Hydrogen is recognised as a distinct substance decades before it is named.

headline: Lavoisier's table of simple substances
detail: Thirty-three bodies that resist further decomposition - the first modern element list.

headline: Davy tears the alkalis apart
detail: Electrolysis yields potassium and sodium in a single week; calcium barium and magnesium follow.

headline: Doebereiner's triads
detail: Groups of three elements whose middle weight is the average of the other two hint at a hidden order.

headline: Spectroscopy turns colour into identity
detail: Bunsen and Kirchhoff read caesium then rubidium straight out of a flame.

headline: Mendeleev orders the elements
detail: Sorted by atomic weight the properties repeat - and the gaps are left deliberately empty.

headline: Gallium lands where eka-aluminium was predicted
detail: Mendeleev corrects the discoverer's density measurement by post. He is right.

headline: Germanium completes the prophecy
detail: Eka-silicon arrives fifteen years after it was described in detail.

headline: Argon: an entire group nobody predicted
detail: An unreactive gas with no place in the table forces a new column - group zero.

headline: Four elements in one year
detail: Neon krypton and xenon from liquid air; polonium and radium from pitchblende.

headline: Moseley: atomic number is the real order
detail: X-ray spectra give each element an integer. The table is re-sorted and the remaining gaps are counted exactly.

headline: Hafnium fills gap 72
detail: Moseley's numbered holes begin to close one by one.

headline: Technetium: the first element made by people
detail: Element 43 never existed in stable form - so it was manufactured.

headline: The first transuranics
detail: McMillan and Abelson push past uranium to neptunium; plutonium follows within months.

headline: Seaborg's actinide concept
detail: Moving the heavy elements into a second f-block row below the table finally makes their chemistry fit.

headline: Mendelevium
detail: Element 101 is named for the man who left the gaps.

headline: The transfermium wars begin
detail: Berkeley and Dubna spend three decades contesting who made elements 104 to 106.

headline: Oganesson
detail: A single atom of element 118 closes the noble gas column.

headline: Period 7 is complete
detail: Nihonium moscovium tennessine and oganesson are named. Every box from 1 to 118 is filled.
